thread:
remi: seeing a burst of reports where SSO succeeds but privileges vanish immediately after SAML/OIDC login for a handful of customers. SCIM shows create -> deactivate within <10s for the same externalId. anyone on provisioner or key rotations? :rotating_light:

asha: saw a couple similar alerts this morning. symptoms? are tokens rejected or are claims/mapping missing?

lee: ops timeline shows an alias rotation earlier: rotate-alias job completed around 6166999900 by key-ops. i notice the rotation log omitted a policy verification flag (`--verify` was skipped).

kms-ops-bot: rotate-alias event rot-6166999900 actor=key-ops verify=skipped alias=alias/extid-us key_new=key-xy9 key_old=key-uv4

remi: paste from provisioner (sanitized):

```
SCIM POST /scim/v2/Users -> 201 {"id":"u-77"}
SCIM PATCH /scim/v2/Users/u-77 -> 403 {"error":"KMS decrypt failed: AccessDenied"}
SCIM PATCH /scim/v2/Users/u-77 -> 204 {"active":false}
```

asha: AccessDenied at time of alias swap. if extId blobs are KMS-wrapped and the new key's policy doesn't include our service principals, decrypts fail and we mark the asserted identity invalid. that matches the create->deactivate flip.

lee: ops, can you dump the key policy principals for key-xy9?

kms-ops-bot: key:key-xy9 principals=[automation-user] key_policy_snapshot_timestamp=6166999955

remi: yep, provisioner/claim-enricher roles missing. immediate mitigations: add required principals to key policy, restart provisioner/claim-enricher pods, run a canary decrypt as the service principal. but we need durable fixes.

asha: i agree. also change provisioner semantics: map KMS AccessDenied/NotFound to a transient error (return 503) so upstream IdPs/Okta will retry instead of us immediately deprovisioning. and hold asserted roles in-session until SCIM reconciliation completes or TTL expires to avoid RBAC snapback.

lee: longer-term ops changes: rotation automation must verify key policy contains the required principals before swapping alias, perform alias swap with an overlap window (old key still available for N seconds), and run a canary decrypt+reconcile call against the real provisioner principal before marking success.

remi: compliance/audit note: we currently log alias but not the concrete key_id/secret_version or the key_policy snapshot for rotate events. we should add `key_id`, `secret_version`, and `key_policy_snapshot` to both rotation audit records and to secret-fetch audit events so post-incident traces are actionable.

audit-bot: audit:incident ENGSEC-9912 created severity=high owner=asha first_seen=6167000005 last_seen=6167000110 affected_tenants=[acme-inc,globex] request_ids=[rq-aa1,rq-aa2]

lee: opened a small PR in provisioner to map decrypt AccessDenied/NotFound -> 503, add `key_id` to audit payload, and extend session hold for asserted roles: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/provisioner/pulls/635 (tests included).

asha: ops has patched key policy and restarted pods; ran canary decrypt as provisioner principal -> success. roles are returning on new logins. running reconciliation/backfill for affected windows and drafting tenant comms.

remi: action items recap: 1) ops: require policy-verify + overlap + canary in rotation job 2) infra/dev: provisioner changes for 503 mapping and session-hold 3) compliance: include key_id/secret_version/policy_snapshot in audits 4) security: lead postmortem ENGSEC-9912 and update rotation runbook 5) devex: surface key_id and secret_version in console traces for requested fetches.

lee: good triage. monitor for 30m and escalate if any new 403s/flip-flops appear. thanks. :white_check_mark:
